paragraphs: In Neath Port Talbot the council's fostering service is Foster Wales Neath Port Talbot, based at Neath Civic Centre and part of the national network of 22 Welsh council fostering services. It looks for carers for children from Neath, Port Talbot, Pontardawe, and those children are also cared for by the services shown above.

The council says there is no minimum or maximum age to foster, that single people and couples can both apply, and that renting is fine as long as you have a spare room and a secure home. Working full time, or not working, does not stop an application, pets are part of the assessment, and smokers should say so honestly. Care can be for a few hours, a weekend or much longer. Through Foster Plus, the council also recruits carers who join a team around a child, backed by its therapeutic team, so the child can live locally near family, friends and school.

Allowances depend on the type of fostering, the number of children and how long you care for them; the council gives the example of two older teenagers bringing in £795 a week. Carers have access to a therapeutic team that includes a psychologist, round-the-clock support, local support groups, IT equipment through the E-Care project, long-service awards, Celtic Leisure membership for the household, the local foster carer association, and paid membership of The Fostering Network and AFA Cymru.

The Welsh minimum allowance for 2026-27 runs from £208 to £260 a week depending on the child's age, with any fee on top. Our Wales page sets out the national rules, and our Swansea and Bridgend pages cover the neighbouring areas. Request an information pack from Foster Wales Neath Port Talbot and speak to one or two of the services above.
